### GetLaunchQueryParam

```ts
sdk.SteamApps.GetLaunchQueryParam(pchKey: string): string | null
```

```cpp
const char * GetLaunchQueryParam( const char * pchKey )
```

> Returns the associated launch param if the game is run via steam://run/&lt;appid>//?param1=value1&param2=value2&param3=value3 etc.
> Parameter names starting with the character '@' are reserved for internal use and will always return and empty string.
> Parameter names starting with an underscore '_' are reserved for steam features -- they can be queried by the game,
> but it is advised that you not param names beginning with an underscore for your own features.
> Check for new launch parameters on callback NewUrlLaunchParameters_t

| Parameter | C++ type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `pchKey` | `const char *` |  |

Valve: <https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/api/ISteamApps#GetLaunchQueryParam>

### GetLaunchCommandLine

```ts
sdk.SteamApps.GetLaunchCommandLine(cubCommandLine: number): { result: number; pszCommandLine: string }
```

```cpp
int GetLaunchCommandLine( char * pszCommandLine, int cubCommandLine )
```

> Get command line if game was launched via Steam URL, e.g. steam://run/&lt;appid>//&lt;command line>/.
> This method of passing a connect string (used when joining via rich presence, accepting an
> invite, etc) is preferable to passing the connect string on the operating system command
> line, which is a security risk.  In order for rich presence joins to go through this
> path and not be placed on the OS command line, you must set a value in your app's
> configuration on Steam.  Ask Valve for help with this.
>
> If game was already running and launched again, the NewUrlLaunchParameters_t will be fired.

| Parameter | C++ type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `pszCommandLine` | `char *` | Output string; buffer size `cubCommandLine`. |
| `cubCommandLine` | `int` |  |

Valve: <https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/api/ISteamApps#GetLaunchCommandLine>
